newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Opel protests Hungary procurement act.
newsitem.headline: Opel protests Hungary procurement act.

text.p: Car maker Adam Opel AG's Hungarian unit is considering legal steps against Hungary's Procurement Act which excludes Opel from all public tenders until the year 2000, the company said on Saturday.
"We think the Procurement Act is anti-constitutional and the management will consider steps on Monday," Andras Danos, the head of Opel Hungary's press office, told Reuters.

Hungary's Procurement Act came into effect in November 1995 excluding all car retailers that in the five years before the act appeared have lost court cases or have been given judgements against by Hungary's Competition Court.

Opel has been found guilty by the Competiton Court in September 1995 of incorporating into the price of some cars a customs duty surcharge that came into effect after the cars were imported, Danos said.
He added, that they have refounded the difference to their clients, but one of them later made a complaint to the Competition Office.
The Prime Minister's office has announced on Friday the winners of a procurement tender were Volkswagen Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz AG and Skoda.
Officials from the Prime Minister's Office were not immediately available, but Danos said the procurement could mean sales of 5,000 to 10,000 cars over the next three years.
The latest complete statistics available show that in the January-April period of 1996, new car sales in Hungary were 19,276, of which 4,047 Opels.
Hungarian Car Importers Association expect total car sales of around 50,000 for the whole year, compared with a 90,000 peak in 1994.
Adam Opel AG is wholly-owned by U.S. car maker General Motors. --Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040
